name: Dried Rusk
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Set a sponge with the milk, yeast, and salt, stirring in flour until you have a thick batter
Early next morning add the well-beaten eggs, and flour enough to enable you to roll out the dough
Let this rise in the bread-bowl two hours
Roll into a sheet nearly an inch thick
Arrange in your baking-pan two deep, laying one upon the other carefully
Let these stand for another half-hour
To dry: divide the twins, leaving one side of each cake soft, and pile them loosely in the pan, set them in the oven when the fire is declining for the night, and leave them in until morning
Put them in a clean muslin bag, and hang them up in the kitchen
They will be fit to eat upon the third day

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Set a sponge with the milk, yeast, and salt, stirring in flour until you have a thick batter
2. Early next morning add the well-beaten eggs, and flour enough to enable you to roll out the dough
3. Let this rise in the bread-bowl two hours
4. Roll into a sheet nearly an inch thick
5. Cut into round cakes
6. Arrange in your baking-pan two deep, laying one upon the other carefully
7. Let these stand for another half-hour
8. Bake
9. To dry: divide the twins, leaving one side of each cake soft, and pile them loosely in the pan, set them in the oven when the fire is declining for the night, and leave them in until morning
10. Put them in a clean muslin bag, and hang them up in the kitchen
11. They will be fit to eat upon the third day
